dedupe_keys.name: critical care unit health digital twin framework with discrete event simulation to track and optimise workflows

description: This case study presents a framework that combines a digital twin with discrete event simulation to optimise workflows in a critical care unit based on real-time changes of state, with an emphasis on patient safety, operational efficiency and sustainability. The authors, from British universities and a hospital partner, published it as an open-access journal article. They propose a dual-layer architecture that monitors physical and conceptual entities in the unit and, in the current scope, use Microsoft Azure cloud services to track treatment workflows in real time from observation forms. The article is free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: the implementation covers workflow tracking, not full optimisation, it relies on data recorded in observation forms, and it was tested in one setting. The study reports that reviewing observation forms alone tracked 72 percent of staff-performed tasks in real time, and argues that digital twins can help bridge the gap between actual and ideal clinical practice. Simulation uses: an example architecture for hospital digital twins feeding discrete event simulation for capacity and operations planning, including under surge conditions. Related records: the HOSPIT'WIN patient pathway digital twin (platform-hospit-win-patient-pathway-digital-twin) and the Yongin Severance IT outage digital twin training (case_study-yongin-severance-hospital-it-outage-digital-twin-training) are comparable hospital digital twins.
